charter:
# Charter — DESIGN-PUBLISH (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** DESIGN-PUBLISH 'Publish the SPEC_V2 studio design pack, live', track programme, ADM phase Preliminary, plateau definition, tranche 0, project `01a1d039-0d39-7414-b43c-450de170ffe1`, programme `01a1d039-0d24-7d16-ae52-4841e96ccfac`, plan `docs/design/STUDIO-SPEC.md` (active). The row records `status: closed`, `meta.measured_status: built`, `meta.viability: rework`, `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]`, `meta.closure_outputs: [closure-review]` and issues 32, 33, 36, 37, 89, 97, 103 and 149. It was reopened at 2026-11-21T17:51:30Z for 'the retrospective MSP/TOGAF/SAFe rework of tranche 0 (#526)' under decision `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Mandate:** publish the studio design pack live — the Project Brief, Evidence and Closure review outputs and the seven Phase A–D artefact documents dated 2026-11-22 — and re-close the project through the one gate.
- **Scope:** the committed pack and its governance records. Out of scope is the republish from live rows, which the rework note assigns to U7; the live public window is 102 outputs against 165 in the pack at the 2026-11-21 record.
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26; it records the lifecycle, it does not authorise new work.

body.assignment: Rework DESIGN-PUBLISH by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts and the eight Phase E–H artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and publish the project-brief and evidence outputs. The work is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26.
body.scope: The published studio design pack and its records: the ten project documents (Project Brief 01a1ff3e-b21f-7453-aec6-03779a26bda0, Evidence 01a1e686-6efd-7683-9d5a-27e5b05081de, Closure review 01a1ff3e-7ef1-717a-8854-c5883a8b68f5 and the seven A–D artefact documents dated 2026-11-22), the scope baseline, the delivery contract and the closure gate. The live-window republish is out of scope; the rework note assigns it to U7.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the pack under the #526 rework delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14; the Architecture Board reviews the A–D set. The delivery contract 01a1ff3c-7aad-7dda-820e-1c7d85fe70a8 is approved by board decision 01a1ff3c-8f0f-7326-b8a7-2de4d2eb6597; the approver 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545 is distinct from the requester 01a1e607-17d9-77d3-98d3-a43a87c4633d.
body.acceptance_criteria: scripts/verify-project.py --project DESIGN-PUBLISH --snapshot <fresh> is green: 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96, and the strict audit on the same snapshot carries no P0/P1 entry for the project. The closure gate 01a1ff3f-cc40-7000-bce5-85f41c4c0b13 is decided by an approver distinct from its requester. The 2026-11-25 acceptance record at 37f99108 is red on 12 mandatory packages; this pack authors their content and does not claim the red cleared before the batch re-runs.
body.contract: This statement sits on the approved scope baseline 01a1ff3e-51c4-75b1-9db1-a2f729dd10b8 (approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545, taken by 01a1e607-17d9-77d3-98d3-a43a87c4633d) and is complemented by the delivery contract 01a1ff3c-7aad-7dda-820e-1c7d85fe70a8. It is retrospective, dated 2026-11-26.

# Benefits Diagram — DESIGN-PUBLISH (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Goals and outcomes

The project serves one goal: the SPEC_V2 studio design is publicly readable, so a decision can be reviewed outside the office that made it. The measurable outcome is the published pack — 165 outputs authored, of which the live public window served 102 on 2026-11-25. Closing the 63-output shortfall is the outcome the benefit depends on.

## Measures

The measure is the count of outputs the public site serves against the pack index, read from the published-outputs projection rather than counted by hand. On 2026-11-25 the index held 165 rows and the site served 102, so the outcome stands at 62% complete; the same instrument reports the value at every tranche review.

## Benefits and sub-benefits

The benefit is Public collaboration (profile 01a1e9df-1592-79a5-839e-037d8fe4251b): a reader outside the programme follows the design without a briefing. It decomposes into the A–D design documents published 2026-11-22, the E–H architecture deliverables authored in this rework on 2026-11-26, and the declared closure outputs. The first is realised, the second is realised here, and the third waited on the six mandatory documents this pack now carries.

documents.body:
# Candidate Solutions — DESIGN-PUBLISH (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Candidates

Two routes were considered for publishing the pack. The first publishes from the committed pack: the 165 outputs as authored in the repository, served through the pack's output index. The second republishes from the live rows, regenerating the public window from the database so that the site matches the estate as it actually runs.

## Criteria

The routes were judged on three criteria: fidelity to the record, meaning a published body matches an approved row; reproducibility, meaning the same output can be regenerated from the repository alone; and completeness of the public window, meaning how many of the pack's 165 outputs are actually served to a reader.

## Options rejected

The live-row route was not executed in this unit. It is assigned to U7 and had not run at the 2026-11-21 record, which is why the public window stood at 102 of 165. This rework therefore took the committed-pack route and records the shortfall as measured rather than glossing it. The live-row route is deferred on its dependency, not rejected as a design.

## Context

Its boundary is the programme record — projects, artefacts, documents, registers, baselines and contracts — together with the published-output index the public site reads. Runtime infrastructure belongs inside the boundary only where that index depends on it.

## Affected organisation

The programme office consumes the closure record and decides the closure gate. The programme architect owns the artefact set under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. The public reader is an external actor who reads the live pages and never touches the record. The Architecture Board reviews the artefact set and the delivery contract.

The record database (PostgreSQL 18, migration 0107 on this lane) holds the projects, artefacts, documents, registers and baselines. The document store (MinIO at minio.internal:8389) backs published bodies; this box cannot reach it, so the replay base keeps the bodies in the database. The snapshot projection is the read model every receipt measures.

# Gap Analysis — DESIGN-PUBLISH (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Baseline

The baseline is the acceptance state recorded on 2026-11-25: the project is closed, its Phase-G review is compliant, and its receipt is red on the mandatory artefact standard with eleven packages open. On the same date the public window served 102 of the pack's 165 outputs.

## Target

The target is a green receipt: sixteen checks pass, no package the project owns stays open on the standard, and the public window either reaches 165 outputs or carries its shortfall with a named owner. The rework's own scope is the mandatory artefact set — the record, not the republication.

## Gaps and work packages

Two gaps are measured. The eleven open packages close from records the factory writes (architecture-artifact and project-registers) and from the four category documents this pack now carries (benefits-diagram, candidate-solutions, project-context-diagram and gap-analysis). The 63-output public shortfall stays U7's: it is recorded with an owner here, not closed by this rework.

scripts/verify-project.py --project DESIGN-PUBLISH --snapshot <fresh> is green with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96, and the strict audit on the same snapshot carries no P0/P1 entry for the project. # Closure review — DESIGN-PUBLISH (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is the published studio design pack with its governance records, and the acceptance the record carries matches it: scripts/verify-project.py --project DESIGN-PUBLISH --snapshot <fresh> is green with 11 checks and 0 failures at d7293f96, the closure gate 01a1ff3f-cc40-7000-bce5-85f41c4c0b13 was decided by an approver distinct from its requester, and the strict audit carries no P0/P1 entry. The evidence is the ten recorded project documents, the scope baseline 01a1ff3e-51c4-75b1-9db1-a2f729dd10b8, the delivery contract 01a1ff3c-7aad-7dda-820e-1c7d85fe70a8 with board decision 01a1ff3c-8f0f-7326-b8a7-2de4d2eb6597, the Phase-G review 01a1ff3f-2d51-7091-bacb-e7a5cb7b016c citing the delegation, and the 37 acts in transcript.jsonl read back by programme-record.py.
